title: A counter and an expression result: when the number changes
goal: Distinguish the result of ++/-- from the new object state, explain unevaluated sizeof, and select the appropriate branch of ?:.

prerequisites.text: Assignment, bool, short-circuit evaluation, and sizeof(type).
Types and safe ranges. Operator overloading is not required.

sections.title: The counter and the expression play different roles
paragraphs: A counter shows 3. We need to record its old number, then obtain the next number after one more increase. Two similar expressions, count++ and ++count, update the same object but produce values at different moments.
Predict the three printed numbers: oldValue, newValue and count. Follow one statement at a time. Looking only at the final count can hide why oldValue is not 4.

reveal.title: Compare your prediction and follow the steps
paragraphs: With int count{3}; int oldValue = count++; count becomes 4 while oldValue receives 3. Next, int newValue = ++count; makes count 5 and gives newValue 5. Keep separate columns for count afterward and expression result so the distinction remains visible.

-- subtracts 1 with the same prefix/postfix distinction. As standalone statements count++; and ++count; leave the same final count because the result is discarded. Choose clarity rather than claiming one form is faster for every type.
Starting at 8, the same increases would produce 8, 10, 10. The self-check reverses the direction: trace the decreases instead of reusing those numbers from memory.

sections.title: One update per statement
paragraphs: Do not combine multiple updates of one object into a puzzle. Forms such as i++ + ++i can have undefined behavior and are unsuitable prediction experiments. Our updates occupy separate full statements, with output afterward.

Range restrictions remain: ++ on the maximum signed int is not permitted merely because the notation is short. Check preconditions first. We use 3…5 safely inside range and explain dangerous boundaries without execution.

sections.title: sizeof obtains a size without increasing the counter
paragraphs: In sizeof(++count) for an ordinary int, the operand is unevaluated and count stays 5. ++count has type int, so its size equals sizeof(int). Compare with == rather than demanding one byte count on every target. This extends the types lesson with an expression rule.

Unevaluated does not mean arbitrary text is valid: sizeof(stillUnknown) fails without a declaration. The compiler needs a valid operand and type. sizeof yields unsigned std::size_t; auto bytes = ... obtains it without an unnecessary cast.

tables.caption: Size and state are separate observations
rows: sizes match; this is not a byte count

sections.title: Only one branch is evaluated
paragraphs: condition ? first : second checks the condition and evaluates first if true or second otherwise. With divisor=0 it selects 0 without evaluating 12/divisor. Zero is only a demonstration default, not a complete input-error report.

Both branches must be valid expressions even though only one is selected. Language rules determine the result type; we use two int branches. We avoid mixed signs and advanced value categories. Multi-statement branches are clearer as a separate if, treated fully next module.

sections.title: Issue no more than the stock allows
paragraphs: requested <= available ? requested : available selects the smaller valid count. A separate assignment reduces available. Two steps expose the rule against issuing more than stock instead of mixing ++ and ?:.

First exclude negatives and values over 100. issued then lies from 0 to available and the remainder is nonnegative. Test requested=0, requested=available, and requested>available. These are distinct contract cases even if two produce the same stdout for a particular stock.

sections.title: Check more than the final number
paragraphs: For ++ record prior state, result, and final state. For sizeof record count before and after plus size equality. For ?: identify the chosen and skipped branches. A final number alone often hides a wrong explanation.

The table at the start is a record of the explained statements, not a live counter. Record your own prediction before running. The self-check changes both the starting value and the direction: use the rule rather than memorizing 3 5 5.

sections.title: Intentional: an unknown name
paragraphs: This is a separate faulty program for examining a diagnostic. It does not replace your work. Locate the cause first, then compare the build failure with a corrected version.
An unevaluated operand must still be valid.

deep.title: Unevaluated does not mean unchecked
deep.text: sizeof(stillUnknown) does not become valid just because its operand is unevaluated. The name must be declared and the expression must be valid. Likewise, both ?: branches must be valid; selection can avoid an unwanted division at run time but cannot hide invalid source syntax.

sections.title: Now solve a different problem
paragraphs: There are 6 items in stock and 9 are requested. Use ?: to calculate issued, then reduce available in a separate statement. Print issued and remaining as shown in the expected report. The 0…100 validation is already provided before the calculation; explain why it must stay there.
Open Practice. Its starter and your current source are separate from the worked examples. Write a prediction before running, then explain the result in your own words.

selfcheck.prompt: counter starts at 8. The program uses counter--, then --counter, then sizeof(++counter). What does the displayed program print?
feedback: Yes: postfix produces 8, prefix produces 6 after the second decrease, and sizeof does not change counter. The final 1 means that the sizes are equal.
The object becomes 7 after the first decrease, but counter-- produces the old 8. The sizeof operand is unevaluated.
The first two values are correct. ++counter inside sizeof for int is not evaluated, so counter remains 6.

practice.title: Allocation from limited stock
practice.task: There are 6 items in stock and 9 are requested. Use ?: to calculate issued, then reduce available in a separate statement. Print issued and remaining as shown in the expected report. The 0…100 validation is already provided before the calculation; explain why it must stay there.
criteria: There are no hidden updates inside ?:; stock changes exactly once after selection.
Validation stays before the calculation. An invalid request prints invalid without issuing stock.
